description.fun: Bronzor is modelled on an ancient Japanese bronze mirror, and objects shaped like it have been dug out of old tombs. Scientists X-rayed it and saw nothing at all inside. Folklore says polishing a Bronzor makes its surface reflect the truth, but Bronzor hates being polished. The pattern on its back is said to hold a mysterious power, and nobody knows which culture it comes from.
description.guide: Bronzor is a Steel- and Psychic-type Pokémon based on an ancient bronze mirror. It floats using a mysterious energy and is found in ancient tombs, and the pattern on its back is said to hold mysterious power. It evolves into Bronzong.
description.tagline: An ancient bronze mirror that hates being polished.

description.fun: Bronzong is a living dōtaku, the ancient Japanese bronze bells once used to pray for good harvests, and people long revered it as a deity that brings rain. One caused a news sensation when it was dug up at a construction site after a 2,000-year sleep, much like real dōtaku unearthed while building a farm road in 1996. Its bell-like cry is said to open holes to other worlds.
description.guide: Bronzong is the evolved form of Bronzor, a Steel- and Psychic-type Pokémon based on dōtaku, ancient Japanese bronze bells. It was worshipped as a bringer of rain and good harvests, and some are said to sleep for 2,000 years.
description.tagline: A 2,000-year-old bronze bell that rings in the rain.
